title: DRAM as lossy mirror of flash: refetch instead of protect
idea: Reverse which copy is authoritative: for clean (read-mostly) pages such as model weights and file cache, a cheap checksum detects errors on reject-grade 1%-BER dies and the line is refetched from the SSD copy.
why: Lets low-grade dies serve large read-mostly footprints, adding usable capacity without new wafers.

title: Thermally drawn preform ribbons shrink centimeter laminates into nanoscale cells
idea: Ideal: draw memory like optical fiber, kilometers at a time. Closest: stack a cm-scale preform of glass, oxide semiconductor and low-melting metal (Sn-Zn or Al alloy) laminates in a cell cross-section, thermally draw it 1000-10,000x into ribbons whose layers shrink to 10-50 nm, then cut and tile ribbons orthogonally into crossbar or gain-cell tiers.
why: 100x: draw towers produce km/hour at ~$0.01/m and define features by geometric draw-down, not lithography; a speculative >=100x $/GB path from abundant glass, oxide and metal. Trades interlayer diffusion during draw, coarse tiling contacts and unproven semiconductor quality.
note: Geometric draw-down replaces litho; doubts: capillary breakup of 10-50 nm layers, semiconductor quality after draw, crossbar contact alignment.

title: Fiber-drawn salami capacitor arrays sliced into wafers
idea: Imposed scarcity: no lithography and no high-AR etch. Assemble a glass preform of millimetre metal-cored, glass-clad coaxial rods, thermally draw and restack-redraw it (as photonic-crystal fiber makers do) until cores reach ~50 nm pitch, then slice the fused bundle into 5 um discs and hybrid-bond them to a CMOS access-transistor wafer.
why: Feature size comes from draw ratio, not EUV; each slice is a sheet of billions of coaxial capacitors with AR ~100 at no etch cost, made from glass and common metals.
note: Pitch from draw ratio, no litho/etch; doubt: draw disorder breaks registration to access transistors and glass dielectric gives low Cs.

title: Hollow-fiber sieving plus pressure swing recaptures fab helium as service
idea: Effect: helium's 2.6 angstrom kinetic diameter lets it permeate polyimide hollow fibers ~100x faster than N2 or Ar. Capture exhaust at chucks, load locks and leak stations, enrich it to 90% through membranes, finish it to 5N by pressure-swing adsorption and refill on site, all sold as helium-as-a-service.
why: Helium chokepoint: 70-90% recovery cuts virgin helium purchases ~5-10x and protects fabs from Qatar-type outages.
note: Membrane+PSA recovery is commercial; service model twist.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling shares the fab forming-gas recycle loop
idea: Combine the chuck's backside-cooling gas with the fab's existing H2 supply: run 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity ~0.18 W/m-K vs He ~0.15) under wafers in etch/CVD, recapture it through a palladium-membrane purifier and return it to the forming-gas anneal header.
why: Eliminates the largest in-fab helium use while Qatar's ~30% is offline; equal or better heat transfer; H2 can be electrolyzed on site in the U.S.
note: H2 conducts as well as He; plasma-side hydrogen effects and safety qualification are the work.

title: Zero-helium wafer cooling with low-pressure hydrogen backside gas
idea: Ideal: etch/deposition chucks that need no helium. Closest achievable: run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling on 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) from on-site PEM electrolysis, with flow-limiting orifices and an N2-purged plenum so any leak stays below the flammability limit after exhaust dilution.
why: Helium: Qatar ~30% of supply offline since March 2026; backside cooling and purge are the dominant fab He uses. Removes ~60-80% of fab helium demand at equal heat transfer, using U.S.-made hydrogen.
note: Low-pressure accommodation coefficient and H2 safety/process interaction.

title: Vacuum-sealed bag: FPGA CXL card compresses memory inline
idea: Stimulus 'vacuum storage bag' (same clothes, a third of the space) -> a 10-person team builds an FPGA CXL memory expander that compresses cache lines inline (LZ4/base-delta hybrid with hardware page metadata), presenting 2-3x more logical capacity than physical DRAM.
why: Does DRAM's job with about half the bits for compressible (mostly cold) data, multiplying scarce DRAM supply per card.
note: CXL compression expanders already pursued by vendors; FPGA demo straightforward.

title: Ion-beam ripple self-patterning writes wafer-wide nanoline arrays without masks
idea: Ideal: line arrays that appear by themselves under a flood beam. Closest: off-normal low-energy Ar+ sputtering of an a-Si or metal hard-mask film spontaneously forms Bradley-Harper ripples at 20-40 nm wavelength, phase-locked by a coarse pre-pattern; transfer them as wordline/bitline gratings and repeat rotated 90 degrees for the crossing grid.
why: 100x: pattern formation costs one broad-beam ion-source step (tens of $k tooling) instead of SAQP/EUV, cutting array patterning per layer >50x and enabling ~$0.1/GB in multi-tier stacks; trades long-range order and line-edge roughness.
note: Maskless self-organized gratings could slash patterning cost; long-range order and LER are far from DRAM specs.

title: Ephemeral memory: data dies before charge does, so never refresh
idea: Inverts 'stored data must outlive cell retention': a refresh-less DRAM tier holds only AI activations, gradients, KV blocks and packet buffers whose lifetime the compiler/runtime proves is below a guaranteed 10-50 ms retention, with hardware write-timestamps that fault any read past the deadline.
why: Zero refresh power in that tier; cells can use ~30:1 instead of 70:1 capacitors, roughly halving mold, fluorocarbon etch gas and ALD precursor per bit, and refresh counters vanish from the periphery.
note: Compiler-proved short data lifetimes enable refresh-free tier and shorter capacitors; weak-cell tail must still meet guarantee.

title: All-oxide CMOS periphery lets memory panels need no silicon chips
idea: Ideal: periphery made from the same cheap film as the cells. Closest: build sense amps, decoders and refresh logic from complementary oxide TFTs (n-ZnSnO with p-SnO or p-Cu2O, all abundant, <=300 C) using bootstrapped dynamic logic to compensate the weak p-FET, so panel memory needs no bonded silicon driver ICs.
why: 100x enabler: periphery is ~49% of DRAM die (Fact 7); moving it onto ~$30/m2 panel layers is required to reach ~$0.1/GB. Trades sensing speed (50-200 ns) and power.
note: Required enabler for panel memory; weak p-type oxide TFTs limit sense speed, margin and power.

title: Wound-film memory: roll-to-roll TFT DRAM coiled like a film capacitor
idea: Ideal: memory sold by the meter. Closest: imprint and print oxide-TFT DRAM arrays on 10 um aluminum/polyimide web at ~10 m/min, wind the web into a cylinder like a metallized-film capacitor, and connect every turn's wordline/bitline buses at the web edges via flame-sprayed 'schoopage' end metallization plus laser-cut edge decoders into parallel banks.
why: 100x: R2R processing ~$2-10/m2; a 1 m x 1000 m roll at 50-100 GB/m2 holds 50-100 TB for ~$10k -> ~$0.1-0.2/GB. Trades volume (a can-sized multi-TB brick), latency and thermal limits.
note: R2R at ~1-2 um2/bit with usable yield, plus per-turn edge bussing, is the doubt; volumetric bricks not dies.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass panels stacked with twenty tiers of oxide-TFT DRAM
idea: Ideal: memory sold like window glass. Closest: use Gen-10.5 display lines (~9.9 m2 panels) to build 2T0C/1T1C tiers from In-free ZnSnO TFTs, Mo/Al lines and planar Al2O3/TiO2 caps (TFT off-current ~1e-21 A/um makes small caps adequate), 4-5 masks per tier with panel nanoimprint at F~0.25 um, 20 tiers stacked at <=350 C.
why: 100x: panel processing ~$25/m2 per tier vs ~$150k/m2 for leading DRAM wafers; at ~0.5 um2/bit (~250 GB/m2/tier) x 20 tiers = 5 TB/m2 for ~$500 -> ~$0.1/GB vs ~$10/GB today. Trades latency (100-300 ns), volume and power; zero EUV, W, Hf, He.
note: Display-line tiers could cut slow-tier $/GB ~10x; doubts: 20-tier yield, panel nanoimprint overlay, 100-300 ns latency.
